target_customer: Consumers who browse and collect images; revenue came from the site itself (advertising implied, not stated)
problem: People wanted a place to discover and collect images around design, creativity and beautiful things without the weight of larger image hosts.
business_model: Ad supported consumer image sharing site (stated only as very profitable by the founder; mechanism not stated)

founders.name: Gabe Ragland
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him a solo founder with no prior mobile experience who built the site in one week in 2009. YC page lists his current role as AI at Stripe. Education not found.

competitors.name: Imgur
competitors.what: Image sharing site named by TechCrunch as the giant dominating the space

competitors.name: Pinterest
competitors.what: Visual pinboard that passed Tumblr in unique visitors per Compete
competitors.traction_then: Passed Tumblr in unique visitors in 2012 per Compete

technical_complexity.rationale: The founder built the first version in a week in 2009; the hard part was serving 30 million monthly page views, which is ordinary scaling work.

defensibility.rationale: Image collections are easy to copy and users could move to Pinterest, Imgur or Tumblr; traffic was the only asset.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pinterest and others grew past it through 2012. The domain now redirects to threadz.com, an unrelated looking site, so the product did not survive as imgfave.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported 30 million monthly page views and 3.3 million monthly unique visitors in August 2012, and a Hacker News thread asked how it differed from reddit, imgur and pinterest. Demand for browsing images was clear; differentiation was not.

branding.domain_note: imgfave.com 301 redirects to www.threadz.com as of this research; how the domain was acquired is not stated.

identity.visual_style: Simple site focused on design, creativity and beautiful things per TechCrunch
identity.voice_and_tone: Fun and casual per the YC description

branding.community_and_virality: 30 million monthly page views and 3.3 million uniques reported in August 2012, which shows reach, but no merch or fan accounts were found.

brand_strength.rationale: Meaningful traffic but a descriptive abbreviation name, little brand press, and commenters struggled to separate it from other image sites.

outcome_analysis: Imgfave was a solo founder image site that claimed to be profitable and had large traffic in 2012 but faced Imgur, Pinterest and Tumblr in the same year. YC marks it inactive and the domain now redirects elsewhere, but no shutdown post or cause is public, so the factors are inferred from the competition rather than stated by the founder.
notes: The YC listing has no website; imgfave.com redirects to threadz.com, which may or may not share ownership. The $20K 2012 round rests on CB Insights alone. The founder says the company was profitable (TechCrunch, unaudited). A third party site gives 2009 as founding year; TechCrunch also says the site launched in 2009. YC lists team size 2 while TechCrunch calls him solo. Cause of closure not public.
